title: Rule Set knowledge
description:
Guiding question: What do these Rules have in common and which Rules belong here?

Rule Set knowledge is the structured companion of a Rule Set definition. It records for whom the bundle exists, what binds its Rules together and the criteria for admitting a further Rule. It never repeats the membership or execution points that the set's configuration defines, only their reasons.

purpose.description: One sentence stating why the Rule Set exists.

audience.description: Which repositories the set is meant for, described by their attributes.

commonality.description: What binds the Rules together. It is the selection principle that tells a member from a stranger.

rules.description: Every member Rule with the reason it belongs to this set. The list must equal the membership defined by the set's configuration.

role.description: What the Rule contributes to the set's purpose and why it fits its commonality.

admission.description: Criteria a new Rule must satisfy to join this set. They let a reviewer decide whether a Rule belongs here, in another set or needs a new one.

excluded.description: Plausible Rules that deliberately stay out of this set.

ruleset.description: ID of the Rule Set that takes over, if one does.

complements.description: Rule Sets that are usually imported together with this one.

execution_points.description: Why the set runs at its execution points. The points themselves stay in the set's configuration.

references.description: Documents or Knowledge artifacts that stand behind the set.
